subject.title: test(durable): prove restart and upgrade safety

question: Should OpenClaw accept this durable agent/subagent coordination stack in core after the upstream durable RFC/runtime PRs, or should the branch wait or be split until that direction is confirmed?
rationale: The PR adds a new core runtime substrate, persisted schema, env knobs, and operator surfaces; automation can review defects, but it cannot choose the durable-runtime product boundary or upgrade policy.

options.title: Wait for upstream stack and proof
options.body: Require the upstream durable RFC/runtime PRs to land or be superseded, then rebase this PR and add exact-head live restart/upgrade proof before merge review.

options.title: Sponsor the stack now
options.body: A maintainer can explicitly accept the stacked core direction and own the compatibility and upgrade risk while asking for the remaining proof before merge.

options.title: Pause or split
options.body: If the durable core boundary is not accepted yet, pause this PR or split it into narrower tests/docs against an already-landed runtime foundation.

recommendation.title: Wait for upstream stack and proof
recommendation.body: Require the upstream durable RFC/runtime PRs to land or be superseded, then rebase this PR and add exact-head live restart/upgrade proof before merge review.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision spans core architecture, state storage, gateway operator surfaces, and roadmap/product direction, and Peter is the clearest repository decision owner from CONTRIBUTING and recent core history.
